problem: Offline-learned image-goal visual navigation (ViNG, ReViND) faces out-of-distribution observations in the real world (illumination/scene changes, accumulated drift), causing localization loss on the topological map, failed navigation and collisions that require human intervention.
motivation: Offline learning from real-world data generalizes better than sim-trained policies, but limited data coverage makes localization loss frequent. Prior recovery methods need online training, LIDAR/SLAM or test-time disengagement data. The paper's observation is that instead of predicting failure events, one can predict whether future states lie in the offline data distribution (anti-novelty) and steer the robot there.
key_idea: When localization is lost, imagine multi-step latent future trajectories with a self-supervised affordance model, score them by RND novelty and other constraints, and execute the least-novel plan to return to familiar places.
insight: Steering toward low-novelty states is a label-free way to recover from OOD situations. Ablation (Table 2) shows each part helps: no affordance 0.70/0.75/0.66 (Garden/Office/Plaza), no RND or RNN 0.76/0.80/0.70, no RND 0.85/0.86/0.75, no RNN 0.86/0.86/0.80, full 0.89/0.92/0.83. RND mainly helps with scenario changes and active initialization, and the GRU history helps with aggressive view changes. The pretrained encoder and relative goal embedding also yield a better IQL policy even without recovery (0.70 vs ReViND 0.61).
method: IQL image-goal agent: offline IQL (expectile value, AWR policy) with image goals, reward -1 per step, 0 at goal and -10 for collision, hindsight relabeling, negative sampling (pairs beyond d_max get V_min) and relative goal embedding z_g - z_t
Representation: VQ-VAE pretrained encoder with layer norm for illumination robustness, then fine-tuned by gradients from Q
Affordance model: conditional decoder psi(z'|z,u) with inverse encoder varphi(u|z,z') trained with forward-inverse cycle consistency and a VIB KL term to avoid shortcuts, with FiLM conditioning
Temporal aggressive prediction: GRU over history of localized latent states gives h_t as the affordance condition, so subgoals outside the current field of view (sharp turns) can be predicted
RND novelty predictor: a predictor network is trained to match a fixed random prior network on dataset latents, and the error gives the novelty T(z)

Recovery planning: sample u from the prior and roll out K-step latent trajectories, then minimize a cost of terminal novelty, optional goal distance, and reachability, transition-probability and aggressiveness constraints, refined with MPPI. Execute the first step with the policy, repeat until the max value over topological map nodes exceeds V_loc
Topological navigation: nodes are offline images, edge costs are learned V values, route search on the graph; the same recovery also supports active initialization at an unknown position

setting.backbone: VQ-VAE encoder + IQL Q/V/policy networks + affordance model with GRU + RND (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Self-collected offline real-world data: about 35 min of expert and collision trajectories per scenario (morning and afternoon) in 3 outdoor scenarios, 480x640 RGB with odometry poses (poses only used for speed labels)
setting.observation: monocular forward-facing RGB (Realsense D435, 69° FoV), wheel odometry only for training labels
setting.privileged: none (a topological map built from the offline dataset is used for localization and planning)

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 scenarios x 3 difficulties x 10 trials each (90 trials)
numbers.extra: Trained on own offline data from the same scenarios; topological map from the offline data; Scout-mini robot
numbers.evidence: Table 1: avg success rates 0.86, avg distance until intervention 160.3

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; results are from the authors' own real-world trials, and success rates are averages over per-difficulty counts out of 10.
results: SCALE with recovery achieves 0.86 average success and 160.3 m average distance until intervention, versus ReViND 0.61 / 73.1 m and ViNG 0.59 / 82.7 m (26% higher success than ReViND, about 2x distance). Without recovery SCALE reaches 0.70 / 102.4 m, and the gains concentrate on medium and hard routes.
limitations: Evaluated only on a small number of real-world trials (10 per difficulty) in three self-collected outdoor scenes, with no standard benchmark or statistical analysis
Requires offline data and a topological map from the deployment environment, so it does not handle fully unknown environments
Only two baselines compared, and no sim or public benchmark results
